[The third chapter: on the rulings of the twenty-eight celestial mansions]

Know — may Allah grant me and you success in obeying Him — that there are matters by which the crescent of each month can be identified in relation to each mansion. Look at the last day of the Arabic month, for the Sun and Moon will be in one mansion. Then determine, at the end of that day, whether it falls in the first, second, or third third of the Roman month, or in the first or second half. Enter the elapsed days of the Arabic month under that third or half, and you will find the mansion in which the Moon is; take note of it. Then enter the elapsed days of the Coptic month across the mansions, and you will know the mansion in which it is.

For example, suppose the crescent is in al-Sharaṭayn on the first night and seven days have elapsed from the Arabic month. If we want to know the mansion in which the Moon is on that day, we count seven mansions from al-Sharaṭayn and arrive at al-Dhirāʿ. We therefore know that the Moon is in al-Dhirāʿ. Apply the same method. This is the form of the circle, as you can see; understand, and you will be guided.

[Discourse on the mansions, their forms, and the rulings connected with them]

The discourse on the mansion of al-Sharṭayn: this is its form, hāʾ hāʾ, and its letter is alif. When the Moon descends in al-Sharṭayn, it is fiery and inauspicious. Perform in it works connected with worldly affairs, corruption, and bloodshed. The sages at this time would incline toward sleep and stillness. Some of them said that in sleep a person sees what frightens him and disturbs his disposition, and that not sleeping at this time is beneficial. If you desire to perform a work, perform works of evil in it for one who deserves them. Whoever is born in this mansion will be highly corrupt. Its incense is pepper and black seed. God knows best.

[Discourse on the mansion of al-Buṭayn]

Its form is hāʾ hāʾ, and its letter is bāʾ. When the Moon descends in al-Buṭayn, which is hot and moist, a righteous spiritual being descends through it into the world by the permission of God, Exalted is He. It is suitable for matters specific to men rather than women. Perform talismans in it; alchemy is sound in it, as is every craft of high rank. It is suitable for beginning the sciences, making rings, engraving, figures and numerals, incantations for illnesses, and treatment. Whoever is born in it will live happy, rightly guided, successful, and beloved by creatures. Its incense is aloeswood, saffron, and mastic. God knows best.

[Discourse on the mansion of al-Thurayyā, and this is its form]

Its form is hāʾ hāʾ hāʾ hāʾ, and its letter is jīm. When the Moon descends in al-Thurayyā, a spiritual being mixed of heat and cold is generated from it into the world by the permission of God, Exalted is He. Perform talismans in it and what is suitable for women; manage suitable medicines and cooling remedies. It is suitable for travelers, who may hope for increased profit. It is suitable for kings, marriage, and the purchase of slave women and male slaves. Everything managed in it is good, because it is the Moon's equilibrium rather than the Sun's, and everything made in it is praiseworthy.

[Pernyataan tentang manzilah-manzilah, bentuk-bentuknya, dan hukum-hukum yang terkait dengannya]

Pernyataan tentang manzilah asy-Syarṭayn: inilah bentuknya, hāʾ hāʾ, dan hurufnya adalah alif. Apabila Bulan turun di asy-Syarṭayn, ia berapi dan sial. Kerjakan di dalamnya pekerjaan-pekerjaan yang berkaitan dengan urusan dunia, kerusakan, dan penumpahan darah. Para hukama pada waktu ini cenderung untuk tidur dan diam. Sebagian dari mereka mengatakan bahwa ketika tidur seseorang melihat hal-hal yang menakutkan dan mengganggu tabiatnya, dan bahwa tidak tidur pada waktu ini bermanfaat. Jika engkau hendak melakukan suatu pekerjaan, kerjakan di dalamnya pekerjaan-pekerjaan kejahatan bagi orang yang memang layak menerimanya. Siapa pun yang dilahirkan dalam manzilah ini akan sangat rusak. Dupanya adalah lada dan habbatussauda. Allah lebih mengetahui.

[Pernyataan tentang manzilah al-Buṭayn]

Bentuknya adalah hāʾ hāʾ, dan hurufnya adalah bāʾ. Apabila Bulan turun di al-Buṭayn, yang bersifat panas dan lembap, turunlah melaluinya ke alam, dengan izin Allah Yang Mahatinggi, suatu makhluk spiritual yang saleh. Manzilah ini sesuai untuk perkara-perkara yang khusus bagi laki-laki, bukan perempuan. Kerjakan talisman di dalamnya; ilmu kimia berjalan baik di dalamnya, demikian pula setiap kerajinan yang tinggi nilainya. Manzilah ini sesuai untuk memulai ilmu-ilmu, membuat cincin, mengukir, membuat bentuk dan angka, merapal untuk penyakit, serta pengobatan. Siapa pun yang dilahirkan di dalamnya akan hidup bahagia, mendapat petunjuk, berhasil, dan dicintai makhluk. Dupanya adalah gaharu, zaʿfaran, dan mastik. Allah lebih mengetahui.

[Pernyataan tentang manzilah al-Thurayyā, dan inilah bentuknya]

Bentuknya adalah hāʾ hāʾ hāʾ hāʾ, dan hurufnya adalah jīm. Apabila Bulan turun di al-Thurayyā, lahirlah darinya ke alam, dengan izin Allah Yang Mahatinggi, suatu makhluk spiritual yang bercampur panas dan dingin. Kerjakan talisman di dalamnya dan hal-hal yang sesuai untuk perempuan; aturlah obat-obatan yang sesuai dan obat-obatan yang mendinginkan. Manzilah ini sesuai untuk para musafir, yang mengharapkan keuntungan tambahan. Manzilah ini sesuai untuk para raja, pernikahan, serta pembelian budak perempuan dan budak laki-laki. Segala sesuatu yang diatur di dalamnya adalah baik, karena ia merupakan keseimbangan Bulan, bukan Matahari, dan segala sesuatu yang dibuat di dalamnya adalah terpuji.

As for the outcome: whoever is born in it will live happily, hate evil, and have a praiseworthy outcome. Whoever is born in it will live happily, hate debauchery, and love the righteous. Its incense is flaxseed and black seed. God knows best.

[Discourse on the mansion of al-Dabarān, and this is its form]

Its form is three dots (• • •), and its letter is dāl. When the Moon descends in al-Dabarān, which is earthy, a spiritual being descends into the world through it, by the permission of God, and separates enmity, hatred, and corruption in the earth. Beware of seeking needs or beginning works in it. Do not make a talisman in it or devise a craft, for all works in it are bad. It is suitable only for burying the dead, burying money, concealing secrets, digging wells, and cutting channels; it is not suitable for anything else. Whoever is born in it will be blameworthy and forsaken. Its incense is sweet pomegranate peel and frankincense.

[Discourse on the mansion of al-Haqʿah]

This is its form: three dots (• • •), and its letter is hāʾ. When the Moon descends in it, it is a mixture of fortunate and unfortunate influences. Work in it especially on antidotes to poisons and their mixtures. Do not devise a craft of the Sun or the Moon in it, plant nothing in it, wear nothing new, and do not marry in it, for its outcome is not praiseworthy. Its incense is aloeswood, frankincense, benzoin, and mastic. God knows best.

[Discourse on the mansion of al-Haqʿah, and this is its form]

This is its form: three dots (• • •), and its letter is wāw. When the Moon descends in al-Haqʿah, it is a fortunate star. Work in it for affection, love, and amity; go out with a fragrant scent; enter upon kings and notables; pursue their needs and whatever you want; associate with brothers; and begin the works you desire. Marry in it, drink medicine in it, buy slave women and horses in it, plant trees, build, measure, weigh, travel, sell, and buy. All of that is highly praiseworthy. Whoever is born in it will live happily and die a martyr. Its incense is qutrub and wormwood seed. God knows best.

[Discourse on the mansion of al-Dhirāʿ, and this is its form]

This is its form: three dots (• • •), and its letter is zāy. When the Moon descends in al-Dhirāʿ, it is airy, fortunate, and gentle. A righteous spiritual being descends into the world through it, by the permission of God, Exalted is He. It is suitable for beginning the sciences and righteous works, meeting scholars and worshippers, making talismans, the arts of naranjiyyāt, entering upon kings, and forming connections with noble people and brothers. Whoever is born in it will be happy, rightly guided, and successful. Its incense is celery seed and flaxseed.

[Discourse on the mansion of al-Nathrah, and this is its form]

This is its form: seven dots (• • • • • • •), and its letter is ḥāʾ. When the Moon descends in it, it is cold, mixed, and fortunate. A spiritual being descends into the world through it, by the permission of God, and produces enmity, hatred, separation, and what resembles that. It is suitable for making talismans and supplicating against enemies, tyrants, rebels, and rancor. A spiritual being also moves in it; hasten there with works involving weapons of war and signaling, because it is bad and suitable for works of evil, as we have mentioned. Whoever is born in it will be unlucky. Its incense is costus and pomegranate peel. God knows best.

[Discourse on the mansion of al-Ṭarfah, and this is its form]

This is its form: three dots (• • •), and its letter is ẓāʾ. When the Moon descends in it, it is a continuously unfortunate star. A spiritual being descends into the world through it and indicates what resembles the foregoing. Do not make a talisman in it, devise a craft, enter upon kings, begin with affection, or work on wisdom. [UNCLEAR: the source's instruction concerning a qasam.] Solitude is better than association, and it rejects all works. Whoever is born in it will be unlucky. Its incense is nadd perfume and saffron. [Discourse on the mansion of al-Jabhah, and this is its form]

This is its form: seven dots (• • • • • • •), and its letter is bāʾ. When the Moon descends in it, it is cold and inauspicious, though closer to rectitude. Begin in it with works of affection, works of closeness, and approval. Moving from one place to another is suitable in it. Shaping iron and wearing it are disliked in it. Whoever is born in it will be skilled, happy, and successful, but there will be some cunning and deceit in him. Its incense is seed.

Know that the Arabs call the mansions al-Anwāʾ. They were given this name because when the setting star falls, the rising star rises. Ketahuilah—semoga Allah memberi taufik kepadamu dan kepada kami untuk taat kepada-Nya—bahwa Allah Yang Mahatinggi telah berfirman tentang dua belas rasi zodiak dan dua puluh delapan manzilah bulan: “Dan sungguh Kami telah menempatkan rasi-rasi di langit dan menghiasinya bagi orang-orang yang memandang”; dan Allah Yang Mahatinggi berfirman: “Mahaberkah Dia yang menempatkan rasi-rasi di langit,” [lanjutan] ayat; dan Dia berfirman: “Yang memiliki rasi-rasi”; dan Dia berfirman: “Kami telah menentukannya sebagai manzilah-manzilah.” Al-burj adalah bentuk tunggal dari al-buruj, dan burj berarti istana; burj juga dapat disebut benteng. Allah Yang Mahatinggi berfirman: “Sekalipun kamu berada dalam menara-menara yang kokoh.” Sebagian ulama berkata tentang firman-Nya, “Mahaberkah Dia yang menempatkan rasi-rasi di langit”: Rasi-rasi itu adalah tempat tujuh planet yang bergerak, dan jumlahnya dua belas. Yang pertama adalah al-Hamal (Aries), lalu al-Thawr (Taurus), al-Jawzaʾ (Gemini), al-Saraṭān (Cancer), al-Asad (Leo), al-Sunbulah (Virgo), al-Mīzān (Libra), al-ʿAqrab (Scorpio), al-Qaws (Sagittarius), al-Jady (Capricorn), al-Dalw (Aquarius), dan al-Ḥūt (Pisces). Al-Hamal dan al-ʿAqrab adalah rumah Mars; al-Thawr adalah rumah Venus; al-Jawzaʾ dan al-Sunbulah adalah rumah Merkurius; al-Saraṭān adalah rumah Bulan; al-Asad adalah rumah Matahari; al-Ḥūt adalah rumah Jupiter; sedangkan al-Jady dan al-Dalw adalah rumah Saturnus. Rasi-rasi ini dibagi menurut empat tabiat, sehingga setiap kelompok terdiri dari tiga rasi dan disebut segitiga. Al-Hamal, al-Asad, dan al-Qaws membentuk segitiga api; al-Thawr, al-Sunbulah, dan al-Jady membentuk segitiga tanah; al-Jawzaʾ, al-Mīzān, dan al-Dalw membentuk segitiga udara; sedangkan al-Saraṭān, al-ʿAqrab, dan al-Ḥūt membentuk segitiga air. Inilah tabel manzilah bulan, rasi, dan bulan-bulan Romawi, dengan bentuk sebagai berikut:

| Mahj | Thurayyā | Ḥaqʿah | Dhirāʿ | Jabḥah | Ṣarfah | Simāk | Kabl | Shawlah | Baldah | Saʿūd | Muqaddam |
| Rashā | Muʾakhkhar | Dabarān | Hanʿah | Ṭarfah | Khurṭān | ʿAwāʾ | Zubānā | Qalb | Naʿāʾim | Bulaʿ | [UNCLEAR: sel sumber kosong] |

Para ahli tafsir berbeda pendapat tentang makna al-buruj. Sebagian berkata bahwa al-buruj adalah istana-istana di langit, dengan dalil firman-Nya: “Sekalipun kamu berada dalam menara-menara yang kokoh.” Ada yang berkata bahwa al-buruj adalah bintang-bintang; ada yang berkata pelita-pelita; dan ada yang berkata pintu-pintu langit yang disebut Bima Sakti. Aku berkata: Ibn ʿAbbās, semoga Allah meridai keduanya, telah menegaskan bahwa yang dimaksud adalah rasi-rasi yang dikenal sebagaimana telah kami isyaratkan—dua belas rasi—dan bahwa Allah, Yang Mahatinggi, membaginya menjadi empat bagian dan tiga serangkai. Rasi-rasi itu dibagi menurut tujuh planet, sebagaimana telah kami sebutkan pada halaman 32. [UNCLEAR: sumber kemudian menjelaskan sebuah gambar yang melibatkan lima bintang.] Gambar itu menunjukkan bagian depannya ke arah barat dan bagian belakangnya ke arah timur, dan itu adalah al-Thawr (Taurus). [UNCLEAR: hitungan dan hubungan berikutnya dalam sumber menyebut tiga, Taurus beserta bintang-bintangnya, dan sebelas bintang di luar Taurus.] Uraiannya mengikuti bentuk yang telah disebutkan sebelumnya untuk Taurus. [UNCLEAR: sumber memuat frasa tentang kepala dan tanduk.] Bentuk itu dipotong menjadi dua bagian untuk perjalanannya, dengan bagian depan mengarah ke timur dan bagian belakang ke barat. Di antara bintang-bintangnya terdapat al-Thurayyā dan al-Dabarān, yang merupakan manzilah bulan.

Yang ketiga adalah al-Jawzaʾ (Gemini), yang dikenal sebagai Si Kembar. Ia memiliki delapan belas bintang, tujuh di luar gambar. Bentuknya menyerupai dua sosok kembar yang berdiri: salah satunya meletakkan tangan di bahu yang lain; kepala dan seluruh bintang lainnya berada di utara, kakinya di tepi timur, dan kedua kaki mereka mengarah ke barat.

Yang keempat adalah al-Saraṭān (Cancer), yang memiliki enam bintang, dengan empat bintang di luar gambarnya. Bentuknya seperti kepiting, bagian depan mengarah ke timur dan bagian belakang ke barat. Selatan berada di belakang Si Kembar. [UNCLEAR: sumber membandingkannya dengan dua anak domba dalam bentuk angka delapan.] Gambarnya tegak, dan di antara bintang-bintangnya terdapat bintang-bintang terang al-Asad (Leo).

Yang kelima adalah al-Sunbulah (Virgo), yang dikenal sebagai Sang Perawan; jumlahnya dua puluh enam [UNCLEAR: satuan yang dihitung tidak disebutkan dalam sumber].

[UNCLEAR: the opening source name is “Nūliyā.”] What lies outside the figure are seven stars. Its figure is [UNCLEAR: a winged young woman or a running figure] with two wings, having lowered its head over al-Ṣarfah, which is a bright star; among its stars is al-Simāk al-Aʿzal, also a bright star.

The sixth is al-Mīzān (Libra), with eight stars. Its figure is upright, and nine stars lie outside the figure. [§] The seventh is al-ʿAqrab (Scorpio), with twenty-one stars; three lie outside the figure, and its figure is upright. Among its stars is Qalb al-ʿAqrab, a bright star. [§] The eighth is al-Qaws (Sagittarius), called the Archer. It has thirty-one stars behind the stars of [UNCLEAR: al-Qurb]. Its figure is an animal composed of a human and a horse, as though it had confined itself up to the neck and had not moved from the nape of the neck; [UNCLEAR: the source then describes a man who has placed an arrow in his bow and is bent over the saddle]. [§]

[UNCLEAR: the source jumps from the eighth sign to the tenth and does not give a ninth-sign section.] The tenth is al-Jady (Capricorn), with twenty-eight stars. Its figure is the front half of a goat, while the rear is [UNCLEAR: described as] a fish extending to its tail. [§] The eleventh is al-Dālī, known as al-Dalw (Aquarius). [UNCLEAR: the source’s count phrase states forty-two stars.] Three stars lie outside the figure. Its figure is a standing man, holding a bucket in one hand; he has overturned it and poured water in front of his feet, while the water descends from beneath it toward the south. It is also called al-Dalw. [§] The twelfth is al-Ḥūt (Pisces), with thirty-four stars; four lie outside the figure. Its figure is two fish whose tails have been joined together. The total of these is three hundred and forty-three.

Aries is the first of the signs, and Taurus is a constellation in the heaven. Gemini is said to extend across the heaven to its middle, and the jawzaʾ of anything is its middle. Cancer is a constellation in the heaven. [UNCLEAR: the source says that Leo and Virgo were not mentioned as constellations in the heaven, and that some did not mention Libra and Scorpio as constellations in the heaven; likewise Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces, while it also says that they are constellations in the heaven.] [UNCLEAR: the final statement identifies al-Jady as a star beside al-Qalb by which the qiblah is known.] God knows best.

[Chapter on the lands associated with each sign]

Know that Aries is associated with Babylon, Persia, and Azerbaijan; Taurus with Hamadan and the Kurds; Gemini with Hājarjān, Gilan, and Sūfān; Cancer with the land of China and eastern Khurasan; Leo with the Turks, Tatars, and neighboring lands; Libra with the lands of the Romans as far as America, the Copts of Egypt, and Abyssinia; Scorpio with the Hijaz, Yemen, and adjacent lands; and al-Waqad [UNCLEAR: the source label is uncertain] with Baghdad as far as Isfahan. Capricorn is associated with Kerman, Oman, Bahrain, and India; Aquarius with Kufa as far as the land of the Hijaz; and Pisces with Tabaristan, Bahrain, Mosul, and Alexandretta. This is the inhabited part of the whole earth. We have mentioned a portion of the regions and what they contain, fully and completely, according to the signs. God knows best.

[Chapter on the division of time into four divisions]

The first is spring, which some people call summer. It was called spring because [UNCLEAR: the source says that spring is made gentle in it]. Some call it autumn because the rain passed through it; its entry is when the Sun reaches the head of Libra. Winter begins when the Sun reaches the head of Capricorn. Summer begins when the Sun reaches the head of Aries, which they call spring. Then comes autumn, beginning when the Sun reaches the sign of Cancer, which they call summer.

[Chapter on the winds and what is said about them]

The first is the north wind, which blows from the direction of the pole. The second is al-Ṣabā, which comes from the sunrise when night and day are equal. Beneath it is al-Dabūr. The Arabs claim that al-Dabūr turns the clouds back, lowers them in the air, and then drives them along. When the clouds are uncovered from it, al-Ṣabā receives them and places some upon others until they become one dense mass. The south wind follows its trailing parts and extends them, while the north wind tears them apart. The third is the south wind, which faces the north, and al-Dabūr, which is faced by al-Ṣabā. God knows best.

[Chapter on what lies between each heaven and the one above it, and the reports transmitted concerning that]

[UNCLEAR: nama pembuka dalam sumber adalah “Nūliyā”.] Yang berada di luar gambar berjumlah tujuh bintang. Gambarnya adalah [UNCLEAR: seorang gadis bersayap atau sosok yang sedang berlari] dengan dua sayap, yang menundukkan kepalanya di atas al-Ṣarfah, yaitu bintang terang; di antara bintang-bintangnya terdapat al-Simāk al-Aʿzal, yang juga merupakan bintang terang.

Yang keenam adalah al-Mīzān (Libra), dengan delapan bintang. Gambarnya tegak, dan sembilan bintang berada di luar gambar. [§] Yang ketujuh adalah al-ʿAqrab (Scorpio), dengan dua puluh satu bintang; tiga berada di luar gambar, dan gambarnya tegak. Di antara bintang-bintangnya terdapat Qalb al-ʿAqrab, yaitu bintang terang. [§] Yang kedelapan adalah al-Qaws (Sagittarius), yang disebut Sang Pemanah. Ia memiliki tiga puluh satu bintang di belakang bintang-bintang [UNCLEAR: al-Qurb]. Gambarnya adalah hewan yang tersusun dari manusia dan kuda, seakan-akan ia membatasi dirinya sampai leher dan tidak beranjak dari tengkuk; [UNCLEAR: sumber kemudian menggambarkan seorang lelaki yang telah memasang anak panah pada busurnya dan membungkuk di atas pelana]. [§]

[UNCLEAR: sumber melompat dari rasi kedelapan ke rasi kesepuluh dan tidak memuat bagian rasi kesembilan.] Yang kesepuluh adalah al-Jady (Capricorn), dengan dua puluh delapan bintang. Gambarnya adalah bagian depan setengah tubuh kambing, sedangkan bagian belakangnya [UNCLEAR: digambarkan sebagai] ikan yang memanjang sampai ekornya. [§] Yang kesebelas adalah al-Dālī, yang dikenal sebagai al-Dalw (Aquarius). [UNCLEAR: frasa hitungan dalam sumber menyatakan empat puluh dua bintang.] Tiga bintang berada di luar gambar. Gambarnya seorang lelaki berdiri yang memegang timba dengan satu tangan; ia membalikkannya dan menuangkan air ke depan kakinya, sementara air turun dari bawahnya ke arah selatan. Ia juga disebut al-Dalw. [§] Yang kedua belas adalah al-Ḥūt (Pisces), dengan tiga puluh empat bintang; empat berada di luar gambar. Gambarnya adalah dua ikan yang ekornya disambungkan satu sama lain. Jumlah seluruhnya adalah tiga ratus empat puluh tiga.

Aries adalah rasi pertama, dan Taurus adalah rasi di langit. Gemini dikatakan membentang di langit sampai bagian tengahnya, dan jawzaʾ dari segala sesuatu adalah bagian tengahnya. Cancer adalah rasi di langit. [UNCLEAR: sumber mengatakan bahwa Leo dan Virgo tidak disebut sebagai rasi di langit, dan bahwa sebagian orang tidak menyebut Libra dan Scorpio sebagai rasi di langit; demikian pula Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, dan Pisces, sementara sumber juga mengatakan bahwa semuanya adalah rasi di langit.] [UNCLEAR: pernyataan terakhir mengidentifikasi al-Jady sebagai bintang di samping al-Qalb yang digunakan untuk mengetahui kiblat.] Allah lebih mengetahui.

[Bab tentang negeri-negeri yang berkaitan dengan setiap rasi]

Ketahuilah bahwa Aries berkaitan dengan Babil, Persia, dan Adharbayjan; Taurus dengan Hamadan dan orang-orang Kurdi; Gemini dengan Hājarjān, Gilan, dan Sūfān; Cancer dengan negeri Cina dan Khurasan bagian timur; Leo dengan orang-orang Turki, Tatar, dan negeri-negeri di sekitarnya; Libra dengan negeri-negeri Rum sampai ke Amerika, orang-orang Qibṭ di Mesir, dan Habasyah; Scorpio dengan al-Ḥijāz, Yaman, dan daerah-daerah di sekitarnya; dan al-Waqad [UNCLEAR: nama wilayah ini tidak jelas dalam sumber] dengan Baghdad sampai Isfahan. Capricorn berkaitan dengan Kirmān, Oman, Bahrain, dan India; Aquarius dengan Kufah sampai negeri al-Ḥijāz; dan Pisces dengan Ṭabaristān, Bahrain, Mosul, dan Iskandarūnah. Inilah bagian bumi yang berpenghuni. Kami telah menyebutkan sebagian wilayah dan apa yang terdapat di dalamnya secara sempurna dan lengkap menurut rasi-rasi. Allah lebih mengetahui.

[Bab tentang pembagian waktu menjadi empat bagian]

Yang pertama adalah musim semi, yang oleh sebagian orang disebut musim panas. Musim itu dinamakan musim semi karena [UNCLEAR: sumber mengatakan bahwa musim semi menjadi lunak di dalamnya]. Sebagian orang menyebutnya musim gugur karena hujan melaluinya; awalnya terjadi ketika Matahari mencapai kepala Libra. Musim dingin dimulai ketika Matahari mencapai kepala Capricorn. Musim panas dimulai ketika Matahari mencapai kepala Aries, yang oleh mereka disebut musim semi. Kemudian musim gugur dimulai ketika Matahari mencapai rasi Cancer, yang oleh mereka disebut musim panas.

[Bab tentang angin dan keterangan mengenainya]

Yang pertama adalah angin utara, yaitu angin yang bertiup dari arah kutub. Yang kedua adalah al-Ṣabā, yang datang dari arah terbitnya Matahari ketika malam dan siang sama panjang. Di bawahnya ada al-Dabūr. Orang-orang Arab menganggap bahwa al-Dabūr mengembalikan awan, menurunkannya di udara, lalu menggiringnya. Ketika awan itu tersingkap darinya, al-Ṣabā menyambutnya dan menumpuk sebagian di atas sebagian yang lain hingga menjadi satu massa yang padat. Angin selatan mengikuti bagian belakangnya dan memanjangkannya, sedangkan angin utara mencabik-cabiknya. Yang ketiga adalah angin selatan, yang berhadapan dengan angin utara; al-Dabūr berhadapan dengannya al-Ṣabā. Allah lebih mengetahui.

[Bab tentang apa yang berada di antara setiap langit dan langit di atasnya, serta riwayat yang dinukil tentang hal itu]

— 29 —

We have already mentioned the doctrine of the ancients concerning the forms of the celestial spheres and what relates to them. As for the doctrine of the scholars of sacred law, these are heavens according to them. Reports have been narrated in the hadith from Ibn ʿAbbās—some say from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib—who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at al-Baṭḥāʾ when a cloud passed over us. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do you know what this is?” We said: “The cloud.” He said: “And al-muzn?” We said: “Al-muzn.” He said: “And al-ʿanān?” We said: “Al-ʿanān,” and we fell silent. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then said: “Do you know how far it is between the heaven and the earth?” We said: “God and His Messenger know best.” He said: “Between them is a journey of five hundred years, and the thickness of each heaven—that is, its thickness—is five hundred [UNCLEAR: the unit is not repeated in the source]. Above the seventh heaven is a sea whose upper and lower bounds are as far apart as the heaven and the earth. Then above them is a world. [UNCLEAR: the next source phrase is garbled and mentions ‘the son of the heaven and the earth.’] God, exalted is He, is above that, and nothing of the deeds of the children of Adam is hidden from Him.” The proof of this is His saying, exalted is He: “God is the One who created seven heavens, and of the earth the like of them.” Thus the distance of all of them is [UNCLEAR: described in relation to] the journey of the children of Adam. As for the angel, he traverses all of it in a single hour; likewise, the devil reaches the earth before the angel reaches the heaven.

It was narrated that Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī, may God be pleased with him, was asked: “How far is it between the heaven and the earth?” He said: “An answered supplication.” He was asked: “How far is it between the east and the west?” He said: “A day’s journey.” Al-Thaʿlabī related from Ibn ʿAbbās: He said: “The Sun rises each year through three hundred and sixty apertures, and the highest aperture does not rise on that day again until the following year.”

I say: The Sun has benefits and indications. Among the indications is that it is one, and its light illuminates all horizons and the whole world. Likewise, the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, is one, and He governs the world. Second, the Sun’s benefits are distant while its arrival is near; and God, exalted is He, is distant from creation in essence but near in answering. Third, its light is withheld from no one; therefore God’s provision is withheld from none of creation. Fourth, its eclipse is evidence of the existence of the Resurrection, along with other things that indicate its darkness. Fifth, the cloud covers it; [UNCLEAR: the source then says that al-Ghāshiyah covered knowledge].

As for its benefits, they are very numerous. First, it is the lamp of the world. The Exalted said: “And We made the Sun a lamp.” Second, it ripens their food and brings their fruits to maturity without cost. Third, it travels from east to west for their welfare. Fourth, it does not remain in one place, lest it harm creation. Fifth, in winter it is in the lower part of the constellations and in summer in their upper part, for the benefit of the world. Sixth, it does not combine with the Moon in its dominion, lest each of them nullify the light of the other.

If you say: It is in the fourth sphere, and the heavens do not veil it, while the cloud veils it. I say: The heavens are subtle, transparent substances, whereas the cloud is dense because it rises from the earth. God knows best.

(Chapter on the Moon, its similitudes, and what is in it)

It was narrated from Abū Hurayrah that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do you see the full Moon when there is no cloud before it?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “Then do you dispute concerning the Sun when there is no cloud before it?” They said: “Yes.” He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then you will see Him in the same way.”

If you say: Why was the example not made with the Sun, since it is brighter and more complete in light, while the Moon’s light comes from it? I say: For two reasons. First, the Sun’s light overpowers the eyes, so one cannot look at it. Second, it was broken for the sake of the Truth, so God, exalted is He, mended it. This happened when Gabriel struck the Moon’s light with his wing. Its heart broke because it had been comparable to the light of the Sun, so God, exalted is He, mended it in two ways. One is that He made eyes look at it in this world every month. The second is that He commanded His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to use it as an example for the greatest and highest things.

If you say: God, exalted is He, said, “The eyes do not perceive Him, while He perceives the eyes.” I say: We do not claim that the eyes perceive Him in the sense of encompassing Him; rather, what is perceived is a ray.

— 29 —

Kami telah menyebutkan mazhab para pendahulu mengenai bentuk-bentuk falak dan hal-hal yang berkaitan dengannya. Adapun menurut mazhab para ulama syariat, semua itu adalah langit menurut mereka. Telah diriwayatkan dalam hadis beberapa kabar dari Ibn ʿAbbās—dan ada yang mengatakan dari al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib—yang berkata: Kami berada bersama Nabi, semoga Allah melimpahkan selawat dan salam kepadanya, di al-Baṭḥāʾ ketika sebuah awan melintas di atas kami. Nabi, semoga Allah melimpahkan selawat dan salam kepadanya, berkata: “Tahukah kalian apakah ini?” Kami menjawab: “Awan.” Ia berkata: “Dan al-muzn?” Kami menjawab: “Al-muzn.” Ia berkata: “Dan al-ʿanān?” Kami menjawab: “Al-ʿanān,” lalu kami diam. Nabi, semoga Allah melimpahkan selawat dan salam kepadanya, kemudian berkata: “Tahukah kalian berapa jarak antara langit dan bumi?” Kami menjawab: “Allah dan Rasul-Nya lebih mengetahui.” Ia berkata: “Jarak antara keduanya adalah perjalanan lima ratus tahun, dan ketebalan setiap langit—yaitu ketebalannya—adalah lima ratus [UNCLEAR: satuannya tidak diulang dalam sumber]. Di atas langit ketujuh terdapat lautan yang jarak antara bagian atas dan bagian bawahnya sama seperti jarak antara langit dan bumi. Kemudian di atas semua itu ada suatu alam. [UNCLEAR: frasa sumber berikutnya rusak dan menyebut ‘anak langit dan bumi’.] Allah Yang Mahatinggi berada di atas semua itu, dan tidak ada sesuatu pun dari amal anak-anak Adam yang tersembunyi bagi-Nya.” Dalilnya adalah firman-Nya, Yang Mahatinggi: “Allah adalah Dia yang menciptakan tujuh langit dan dari bumi yang semisal dengannya.” Dengan demikian, jarak seluruhnya [UNCLEAR: digambarkan dengan mengaitkannya pada] perjalanan anak-anak Adam. Adapun malaikat, ia menembus seluruhnya dalam satu jam; demikian pula setan mencapai bumi sebelum malaikat mencapai langit.

Telah diriwayatkan bahwa Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī, semoga Allah meridainya, ditanya: “Berapa jarak antara langit dan bumi?” Ia menjawab: “Sebuah doa yang dikabulkan.” Ia ditanya: “Berapa jarak antara timur dan barat?” Ia menjawab: “Perjalanan satu hari.” Al-Thaʿlabī meriwayatkan dari Ibn ʿAbbās: Ia berkata: “Matahari terbit setiap tahun melalui tiga ratus enam puluh celah, dan celah yang paling tinggi tidak menjadi tempat terbitnya pada hari itu lagi sampai tahun berikutnya.”

Aku berkata: Matahari memiliki manfaat dan tanda-tanda. Di antara tanda-tandanya adalah bahwa ia satu, dan cahayanya menerangi seluruh ufuk serta seluruh alam. Demikian pula Sang Pencipta, Mahasuci dan Mahatinggi Dia, adalah satu dan Dia mengatur alam. Kedua, manfaat Matahari jauh, sedangkan sampainya dekat; dan Allah Yang Mahatinggi jauh dari makhluk menurut Zat-Nya, tetapi dekat dalam mengabulkan. Ketiga, cahayanya tidak ditahan dari seorang pun; karena itu rezeki Allah tidak ditahan dari seorang pun di antara makhluk. Keempat, gerhananya adalah bukti adanya Hari Kiamat, serta hal-hal lain yang menunjukkan kegelapannya. Kelima, awan menutupinya; [UNCLEAR: sumber kemudian mengatakan bahwa al-Ghāshiyah menutupi pengetahuan].

Adapun manfaatnya sangat banyak. Pertama, ia adalah pelita alam. Allah Yang Mahatinggi berfirman: “Dan Kami menjadikan Matahari sebagai pelita.” Kedua, ia mematangkan makanan mereka dan mematangkan buah-buahan mereka tanpa biaya. Ketiga, ia bergerak dari timur ke barat demi kemaslahatan mereka. Keempat, ia tidak berhenti di satu tempat agar tidak membahayakan makhluk. Kelima, pada musim dingin ia berada di bagian bawah rasi-rasi dan pada musim panas di bagian atasnya demi manfaat alam. Keenam, ia tidak berkumpul bersama Bulan dalam kekuasaannya agar masing-masing tidak membatalkan cahaya yang lain.

Jika engkau berkata: Matahari berada di falak keempat, langit tidak menghalanginya, tetapi awan menghalanginya. Aku berkata: Langit adalah substansi yang halus dan transparan, sedangkan awan bersifat padat karena naik dari bumi. Allah lebih mengetahui.

(Bab tentang Bulan, perumpamaannya, dan apa yang ada di dalamnya)

Diriwayatkan dari Abū Hurayrah bahwa ia berkata: Nabi, semoga Allah melimpahkan selawat dan salam kepadanya, bersabda: “Apakah kalian melihat Bulan purnama ketika tidak ada awan di hadapannya?” Mereka menjawab: “Ya.” Ia berkata: “Apakah kalian memperdebatkan Matahari ketika tidak ada awan di hadapannya?” Mereka menjawab: “Ya.” Ia, semoga Allah melimpahkan selawat dan salam kepadanya, berkata: “Maka kalian akan melihat-Nya dengan cara yang sama.”

Jika engkau berkata: Mengapa perumpamaan tidak dibuat dengan Matahari, padahal ia lebih terang dan lebih sempurna cahayanya, sedangkan cahaya Bulan berasal darinya? Aku berkata: Karena dua perkara. Pertama, cahaya Matahari mengalahkan penglihatan sehingga seseorang tidak mampu memandangnya. Kedua, ia pecah demi kebenaran, lalu Allah Yang Mahatinggi memperbaikinya. Hal itu terjadi ketika Jibril memukul cahaya Bulan dengan sayapnya. Hatinya pecah karena sebelumnya menyerupai cahaya Matahari, lalu Allah Yang Mahatinggi memperbaikinya dengan dua hal. Pertama, Dia menjadikan mata-mata dapat memandangnya di dunia setiap bulan. Kedua, Dia memerintahkan Nabi-Nya, Muḥammad, semoga Allah melimpahkan selawat dan salam kepadanya, untuk menjadikannya perumpamaan bagi perkara-perkara yang paling agung dan paling tinggi.

Jika engkau berkata: Allah Yang Mahatinggi berfirman, “Penglihatan tidak dapat mencapai-Nya, sedangkan Dia mencapai penglihatan.” Aku berkata: Kami tidak mengklaim bahwa penglihatan mencapai-Nya dalam arti meliputi-Nya; melainkan, yang dicapai adalah secercah cahaya.

[UNCLEAR: the source continues its discussion of sight, stating that the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, is beyond our existence or our ability to encompass Him.] The Moon has benefits. al-Sharṭayn, al-Buṭayn, al-Thurayyā, al-Dabarān, al-Ḥaqʿah, al-Hanʿah, al-Dhirāʿ, al-Nathrah, al-Ṭarfah, al-Jabhah, al-Khurthān, al-Ṣarfah, al-ʿAwāʾ, al-Simāk, al-Ghafr, al-Zubānā, al-Iklīl, al-Qalb, al-Shawlah, al-Naʿāʾim, al-Baldah, al-Suʿūd, Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, Saʿd Bulaʿ, al-Akhbiyah, al-Muqaddam, al-Muʾakhkhar, and al-Rashā.

(Section on the four stars, their indications, and their management)

The Exalted said: “It is He who made the stars for you, so that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea”; and the Exalted said: “And by the star they are guided.” It was narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with him, that he said: “The knowledge of the stars is lofty and beneficial; many people have been incapable of it.” [UNCLEAR: the source then points to knowledge of the stars for rulings associated with sacred restrictions.]

They agreed that the light of the Moon comes from the light of the Sun, but differed concerning the known stars, which are twenty-two stars. Among them is al-Jady, one of the indications used to determine the qiblah. Al-Jady is a star beside the North Pole. Around it are six small stars, three above and three below. One pair is al-Farqadān, and among the other stars is a bright star facing them. Between them and that star are six small stars, three above and three below, which revolve around the pole. [UNCLEAR: the source’s grammar about al-Jady’s remaining fixed and the relation of these stars is difficult.] Al-Jady is used to identify the pole; al-Jady is the pole of this [UNCLEAR: constellation called al-Firāshah]. It is also said that the pole is its pole.

Al-Jady is used to identify it when there is no Moon. When the Moon is bright, [UNCLEAR: the source says that only a sharp-eyed person can see it]. Al-Suhā is beside it, a faint star by which people test their eyesight. The al-Jady used to identify the qiblah is the Jady of Banāt Naʿsh. [UNCLEAR: the source then refers to three Banāt making four, to two preceding stars, and places al-Jady among the Banāt as their last.]

Al-Suhā is a faint star among Banāt Naʿsh. Hence the proverb: “Show her al-Suhā and she will see the Moon.” The method of knowing the qiblah is to place it behind your back in the land of al-Shām; in Iraq, opposite the back of your right ear; and in Egypt, behind the left [ear], above it. [UNCLEAR: the source then says that one faces the House’s door toward the Station.] Whenever you turn your back toward al-Farqadān or Banāt Naʿsh, you face the direction of the Kaʿbah.

The al-Farqadān are two bright stars close to the pole. Banāt Naʿsh are seven stars: four of them are the bier, and three are the daughters. The same applies to the Lesser Banāt Naʿsh. The North and South Poles are not reached by the Sun or the Moon.

The South Pole has its [UNCLEAR: corresponding] Jady. Suhayl rises, but it appears only in the Arabian Peninsula. Suhayl is beside the South Pole; its rising is from the direction of the south wind, then it moves toward the west, enters the qiblah of the place of prayer, and sets there. Suhayl is a solitary star, separate from the Yemeni stars. Its rising is to the left of the qiblah. It is seen throughout the Arab lands, in Iraq and al-Shām, but it is not seen in the lands of Armenia. [UNCLEAR: the source says that al-Ḥijāz is associated with its rising.] Its sighting in Iraq lasts some ten-odd nights.

Some said: “Suhayl is the star of the Arabs.” They say: “When Suhayl rises, do not feel safe from the torrent.” Know that the stars number one thousand and twenty-two. [UNCLEAR: the source’s final phrase says something about a tenth of a star in twelve and is not clear.]

Amirul Mukminin ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, semoga Allah memuliakan wajahnya, berkata: “Tidur telanjang di bawah Bulan menyebabkan kusta. Apabila pakaian dicuci lalu dijemur di bawah cahaya Bulan, pakaian itu akan mudah rusak dan warnanya berubah.” Allah lebih mengetahui.

(Bab: Bulan bergeser setiap malam ke salah satu manzilah, dan inilah nama-namanya)

al-Sharṭayn, al-Buṭayn, al-Thurayyā, al-Dabarān, al-Ḥaqʿah, al-Hanʿah, al-Dhirāʿ, al-Nathrah, al-Ṭarfah, al-Jabhah, al-Khurthān, al-Ṣarfah, al-ʿAwāʾ, al-Simāk, al-Ghafr, al-Zubānā, al-Iklīl, al-Qalb, al-Shawlah, al-Naʿāʾim, al-Baldah, al-Suʿūd, Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, Saʿd Bulaʿ, al-Akhbiyah, al-Muqaddam, al-Muʾakhkhar, dan al-Rashā.

(Bab tentang empat bintang, tanda-tandanya, dan pengaturannya)

Allah Yang Mahatinggi berfirman: “Dialah yang menjadikan bintang-bintang untuk kalian agar kalian mendapat petunjuk dengannya dalam kegelapan darat dan laut”; dan Dia berfirman: “Dan dengan bintang mereka mendapat petunjuk.” Diriwayatkan dari Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, dari Ibn ʿAbbās, semoga Allah meridainya, bahwa ia berkata: “Ilmu tentang bintang-bintang adalah tinggi dan bermanfaat; banyak orang tidak mampu menguasainya.” [UNCLEAR: sumber kemudian menunjuk pada pengetahuan tentang bintang untuk hukum-hukum yang berkaitan dengan larangan-larangan suci.]

Mereka sepakat bahwa cahaya Bulan berasal dari cahaya Matahari, tetapi mereka berbeda pendapat tentang bintang-bintang yang dikenal, yang berjumlah dua puluh dua bintang. Di antaranya adalah al-Jady, salah satu petunjuk yang digunakan untuk menentukan kiblat. Al-Jady adalah bintang di samping Kutub Utara. Di sekelilingnya terdapat enam bintang kecil, tiga di atas dan tiga di bawah. Salah satu pasangannya adalah al-Farqadān, dan di antara yang lainnya terdapat bintang terang yang berhadapan dengannya. Di antara keduanya dan bintang itu terdapat enam bintang kecil, tiga di atas dan tiga di bawah, yang berputar mengelilingi kutub. [UNCLEAR: tata bahasa sumber tentang al-Jady yang tetap dan hubungan bintang-bintang ini sulit dipahami.] Al-Jady digunakan untuk menunjukkan kutub; al-Jady adalah kutub dari [UNCLEAR: rasi yang disebut al-Firāshah] ini. Ada pula yang mengatakan bahwa kutub adalah kutubnya.

Al-Jady digunakan untuk mengenalinya ketika tidak ada Bulan. Ketika Bulan terang, [UNCLEAR: sumber mengatakan bahwa hanya orang yang penglihatannya tajam yang dapat melihatnya]. Al-Suhā berada di sampingnya, yaitu bintang samar yang digunakan orang-orang untuk menguji penglihatan mereka. Al-Jady yang digunakan untuk mengetahui kiblat adalah Jady dari Banāt Naʿsh. [UNCLEAR: sumber kemudian menyebut tiga Banāt yang menjadi empat, dua bintang yang mendahului, dan menempatkan al-Jady di antara Banāt sebagai yang terakhir.]

Al-Suhā adalah bintang samar di dalam Banāt Naʿsh. Karena itu ada peribahasa: “Tunjukkan kepadanya al-Suhā, maka ia akan melihat Bulan.” Cara mengetahui kiblat adalah menempatkan bintang itu di belakang punggungmu di wilayah al-Shām; di Irak, tepat berhadapan dengan bagian belakang telinga kananmu; dan di Mesir, di belakang [telinga] kiri, di atasnya. [UNCLEAR: sumber kemudian mengatakan bahwa seseorang menghadap pintu Bait menuju Maqām.] Apabila engkau membelakangi al-Farqadān atau Banāt Naʿsh, engkau menghadap arah Kaʿbah.

Al-Farqadān adalah dua bintang terang yang dekat dengan kutub. Banāt Naʿsh berjumlah tujuh bintang: empat di antaranya adalah keranda dan tiga adalah anak-anak perempuan. Demikian pula Banāt Naʿsh al-Ṣughrā. Kutub Utara dan Kutub Selatan tidak dicapai oleh Matahari maupun Bulan.

Kutub Selatan memiliki Jady [UNCLEAR: yang bersesuaian dengannya]. Suhayl terbit, tetapi tidak tampak kecuali di Jazirah Arab. Suhayl berada di samping Kutub Selatan; terbitnya berasal dari arah angin selatan, kemudian bergerak ke arah barat, berada di arah kiblat tempat salat, dan terbenam di sana. Suhayl adalah bintang tunggal yang terpisah dari bintang-bintang Yaman. Terbitnya berada di sebelah kiri kiblat. Ia terlihat di seluruh negeri Arab, di Irak dan al-Shām, tetapi tidak terlihat di negeri Armenia. [UNCLEAR: sumber mengatakan bahwa al-Ḥijāz berkaitan dengan terbitnya.] Di Irak, Suhayl terlihat selama sekitar sepuluh malam lebih.

Sebagian orang berkata: “Suhayl adalah bintang orang-orang Arab.” Mereka mengatakan: “Apabila Suhayl terbit, jangan merasa aman dari banjir.” Ketahuilah bahwa jumlah bintang adalah seribu dua puluh dua. [UNCLEAR: frasa terakhir sumber menyebut sesuatu tentang sepersepuluh bintang dalam dua belas dan tidak jelas.]

[UNCLEAR: the source opens with the phrase “ten figures.”] It describes figures along the path of the Sun, namely the twelve zodiac signs. Among them are three hundred and sixty stars in twenty-one figures inclined away from the Sun’s path toward the north. These include the Great Bear, the Lesser Bear, the Dragon, and others. Among them are three hundred and sixteen stars in fifteen figures inclined away from the Sun’s path. It resembles a standing bear stretching out its paws. It has seven stars, and the Arabs call it the Lesser Banāt Naʿsh. Four stars form the bier in a square, and three lie on its tail. Eight stars lie outside the figure. Among them are seven stars that the Arabs classify as the Lesser Banāt Naʿsh, the stars observed toward the North Pole. [UNCLEAR: the source’s overlapping seven- and eight-star descriptions are retained as stated.]

I say: Among them is the Great Bear, with twenty-seven stars. Eight stars lie outside the figure. Among them are seven stars that the Arabs call Banāt Naʿsh: four on its body and three on its tail. The Arabs call them al-Suhā. Among them is the Dragon, with thirty-one stars. Its figure is a great serpent with many coils. It begins with four stars arranged as an inclined square at its head. [UNCLEAR: the source’s phrase following the head-and-scorpion description is garbled.] The Dragon is a place in the heaven, a kind of serpent, and the greatest of them.

Among them is al-Fakkah, called the Northern Crown. [UNCLEAR: the source gives a garbled description of a kind of heavenly serpent and eight stars associated with its roundness.] Al-Fakkah also consists of round stars behind al-Simāk al-Rāmiḥ.

Among them is the Kneeling Man, whose figure has twenty-seven stars. Among them are al-Sabʿāt, also called al-Lawz and al-Ṣubḥ al-Rūmī. Among them is the Tortoise, whose stars number ten; some of its stars are drawn as al-Nasr al-Wāqiʿ. There is also the Hen, which has nineteen stars; two stars lie outside the figure, and its largest stars are in the Milky Way. Among them is the Triangle, four stars between the star of the Fish and the Eagle above the head of al-Ghūl. Thus the total of these northern figures is three hundred and sixty stars.

As for the southern figures, they comprise three hundred and twelve stars. Among them is [UNCLEAR: Qayqaṭus], with twenty-two stars. Its figure is a bare animal with two legs and a tail like the tail of a whale. Among them is al-Jabbār (Orion), with thirty-eight stars. Its figure is a running man holding a staff, with a belt and a sword at his middle. Among its stars is al-Jawzāʾ, a red star. There are also twelve stars gathered beneath Orion’s leg, resembling a rabbit whose face is toward the west and whose rear is toward the east.

Among them is the Great Dog, with twenty-eight stars; eleven stars lie outside the figure, behind the stars of al-Jawzāʾ. [UNCLEAR: the source’s relation between al-Sunbulah and the stars of al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr is obscure; it calls one al-Abbān al-Marzabān.] Among them is al-Shiʿrā al-Ghumaysāʾ, the stars that rise after al-Jawzāʾ. As for Cancer, [UNCLEAR: the source refers to figures in al-Jawzāʾ and to al-Shiʿrā al-Ghumaysāʾ in the arm]. The Arabs claim that the two are the sisters of Suhayl.

Among them is the Southern Crown, with thirteen stars; six stars lie outside the figure. Its figure is a great fish, with its stars south of the star al-Dālī, its head toward the east and its tail toward the west. Among them is the Milky Way, [UNCLEAR: the source’s location phrase is garbled]. This is a summary of the southern and northern stars.

I say: What some authors have mentioned is restricted to the famous stars. As for the less famous stars, they are very numerous; they will be mentioned later, if God the Exalted wills.

— 32 —

[Chapter on their bodies and what is connected to them]

Know that the Sun’s body is one hundred and a half times the measure of the world, and the Moon’s body is thirty-nine times the measure of the world. The same applies to Venus, Mercury, and Mars. Jupiter’s body is eighty-two times the measure of the world, and Saturn’s body is ninety-nine times the measure of the world. Some of our scholars said that the Sun’s body extends fifteen degrees before it and likewise behind it; the Moon’s body extends twelve degrees before it and likewise behind it; Mars’s body extends eight degrees behind it and likewise before it; Venus’s body extends seven degrees before it and likewise behind it; and Mercury’s body is likewise. God, exalted is He, knows best.

[Chapter: every star in the heaven is many times the measure of the world]

As for the fixed stars, there are fifteen of them, including al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr, al-Simāk, al-Nasr al-Ṭāʾir, Qalb al-Asad, and similar stars. Each of these stars is sixty-four times the measure of the world.

[Chapter on the seven stars traversing the spheres]

Know that the Moon traverses the sphere in twenty-nine days and one-third of a day; Mercury traverses it in twenty-eight days; Venus traverses it in two hundred and twenty-four days and one-quarter of a day; the Sun traverses it in three hundred and sixty-five days and one-quarter of a day; Mars traverses it in six hundred and thirty [UNCLEAR: the source omits the unit]; Jupiter traverses it in eleven years; and Saturn traverses it in twenty-nine years. [Chapter on the stations of the zodiac signs]

Know that the Moon’s station in each sign is two days and three nights; Mercury’s station in each sign is fifteen days; Venus’s station in each sign is twenty-five days; Jupiter’s station in each sign is one year; and Saturn’s station in each sign is thirty months.

[Chapter on the dignity of the planets]

Know that the Moon’s dignity is Taurus; Mercury’s dignity is Virgo; Venus’s dignity is Pisces; the Sun’s dignity is Aries; Mars’s dignity is Capricorn; Jupiter’s dignity is Cancer; and Saturn’s dignity is Libra. As for the Pleiades, it is said that they are the lamp of the world in the heaven because they are a gathering of stars like a knot. They are in the heaven, and the Arabs call them “the stars,” because there is no place in the heaven with more stars than them.

[Chapter on the day belonging to each of the seven planets]

Sunday belongs to the Sun; Monday to the Moon; Tuesday to Mars; Wednesday to Mercury; Thursday to Jupiter; Friday to Venus; and Saturday to Saturn.

[Chapter on the conjunction of the planets]

The meaning of conjunction is that one planet is in a sign while the other is in its counterpart. “Meeting” means that the two come together in one sign. (Chapter on the natures of the planets)

Know that the Moon is cold and feminine. [UNCLEAR: the source’s wording associates it with phlegm and an accidental heat because its light comes from the Sun.] Its influence is laughter and adornment, and it has yellow bile. Mercury is masculine and feminine; it is sometimes fortunate and sometimes unfortunate, and its nature combines heat in balance. Its influence is speech and writing.

Venus is feminine and fortunate, cold and moist. It has phlegm, and its influence is marriage and joy. It is associated with desire, arranging the crown, affectation, bringing hearts together, women, beauty, amusement, and laughter.

The Sun is masculine, hot, and dry. It has yellow bile. It is fortunate by aspect and unfortunate by opposition. Its substance is gold, and its influence is over the sciences. It has the highest dignity, joy, delight, and kingship.

Mars is feminine, hot, and dry. It has yellow bile; its substance is iron and its taste is bitter. Its influence is over the head, the stomach, killing, women, and other things.

Jupiter is masculine, moderate, spiritual, and fortunate. It has blood; its substance is tin; its taste and color are white. Its influence is over the wind residing in the heart, and it brings abundant gifts and leadership.

Saturn is masculine, cold, dry, and dark. It has black bile; its substance is lead; its taste is bitter and its color black. Its influence is over study and deliberation, and it is associated with heat, injustice, subjugation, and coercion.

I say: Some people claimed that these zodiac signs, spheres, and moving planets exert influence in the world and govern the worlds. They used as evidence His saying, exalted is He: “By those who direct an affair,” and similar passages. [UNCLEAR: the author’s transition here is damaged.] It has been transmitted that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended to heaven, he informed us about the zodiac signs, the stars, and other matters. Rather, proofs and evidence establish that the Creator, exalted is He, invented and brought them into being.

As for His saying, exalted is He, “By those who direct an affair,” Ibn ʿAbbās said that some angels are entrusted with provisions, some with rain, and some with the winds, as is mentioned in the creation of the angels. If they are directors, then they direct only by the permission of the Creator, majestic and exalted is He, because He is the Powerful, the Knowing, and the Wise. It is narrated that the books sent down from heaven to earth number one hundred and four: the scrolls of Seth, sixty; the scrolls of Abraham, thirty; the scrolls of Moses before the Torah, ten; the Torah; the Gospel; the Psalms; and the Furqān. Matahari bersifat maskulin, panas, dan kering. Ia memiliki empedu kuning. Ia membawa keberuntungan melalui aspek dan kesialan melalui oposisi. Zatnya adalah emas, dan pengaruhnya atas ilmu-ilmu. Ia memiliki kemuliaan tertinggi, kegembiraan, kesenangan, dan kerajaan.

Mars bersifat feminin, panas, dan kering. Ia memiliki empedu kuning; zatnya adalah besi dan rasanya pahit. Pengaruhnya atas kepala, perut, pembunuhan, perempuan, dan hal-hal lainnya.

Jupiter bersifat maskulin, seimbang, ruhani, dan membawa keberuntungan. Ia memiliki darah; zatnya adalah timah; rasa dan warnanya putih. Pengaruhnya atas angin yang berdiam di dalam hati, dan ia membawa pemberian yang melimpah serta kepemimpinan.

Saturnus bersifat maskulin, dingin, kering, dan gelap. Ia memiliki empedu hitam; zatnya adalah timah hitam; rasanya pahit dan warnanya hitam. Pengaruhnya atas belajar dan perenungan, dan ia berkaitan dengan panas, kezaliman, penundukan, dan pemaksaan.

It is narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “The distance between the basmalah, ‘In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful,’ and the Greatest Name of God is only like the distance between the whiteness of the eye and its blackness.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, also said: “There is nothing between human beings and the devils except the basmalah, ‘In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.’ It is the concealed name indicating that what follows it is the Greatest Name, namely God, because the Greatest Name is the Name of Majesty. It is the pole of the names, and they return to it. Among the names it is like a proper name: if you ask by the Most Compassionate, you say ‘God,’ and likewise the other names are attached to it and known through its majesty and exalted elevation.

“It has an additional distinction over the other names: if you remove the letter alif from it, ‘lillah’ remains; if you remove the first lām, ‘lah’ remains; and if you remove the second as well, ‘huwa’ remains. Isrāfīl is the bearer of the Trumpet and the blowing. He has three blasts: the blast of terror, of which the Most High said, “Then those in the heavens and those on the earth were terrified”; the blast of swooning, of which the Most High said, “Then those in the heavens and those on the earth swooned”; and the blast of resurrection, of which the Most High said, “Then it is blown into it again, and behold, they are standing and looking.” Each blast has matters peculiar to it.

ʿIzrāʾīl, peace be upon him, is entrusted with taking the souls and bringing about their extinction. Through him tyrants are subdued and the roots of the disbelievers and the arrogant are cut off. Through him the believer finds rest, reaches his Lord, and rejoices in what God has prepared for him of generosity, bounty, pardon, and forgiveness.

Mīkāʾīl, peace be upon him, is entrusted with the provisions and sustenance of God’s servants and with preserving their existence. There is no sesame seed on earth without an angelic helper assigned to it for its owner. Jibrīl, peace be upon him, has assistants too numerous to count, and he has invocations and works that distinguish them from one another.

These four are kings of days, with particular days assigned to them. Jibrīl, peace be upon him, has Monday because it is cold and moist. Isrāfīl, peace be upon him, has Thursday, which is hot and moist. ʿIzrāʾīl, peace be upon him, has Saturday because it is cold and moist; [UNCLEAR: the source then associates his domain with earth, death, and extinction]. Isrāfīl adalah pembawa sangkakala dan peniupan. ʿIzrāʾīl, semoga keselamatan atasnya, ditugaskan mengambil ruh-ruh dan menyebabkan kefanaannya. Melaluinya para tiran ditundukkan dan akar orang-orang kafir serta orang-orang sombong diputus. Melaluinya orang beriman memperoleh ketenteraman, sampai kepada Tuhannya, dan bergembira atas apa yang Allah siapkan baginya berupa kemurahan, kedermawanan, pemaafan, dan ampunan.

Mīkāʾīl, semoga keselamatan atasnya, ditugaskan mengurus rezeki dan penghidupan para hamba Allah serta menjaga keberadaan mereka. Isrāfīl, semoga keselamatan atasnya, memiliki hari Kamis, yang panas dan lembap. ʿIzrāʾīl, semoga keselamatan atasnya, memiliki hari Sabtu karena hari itu dingin dan lembap; [UNCLEAR: sumber kemudian mengaitkan wilayahnya dengan tanah, kematian, dan kefanaan]. Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm was written upon Adam’s forehead five hundred years before he was created. Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm was written upon Gabriel’s wing on the day he descended upon Abraham, peace be upon them both. He said: “In the name of God: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham.” Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm was also written upon Moses’ staff, peace be upon him. Its writing was in Syriac, and were it not for it, the sea would not have split for him.

Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm was on Jesus’ tongue, peace be upon him, when he spoke in the cradle. He would recite it over the dead, and they would come to life by the permission of God Most High. Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm was written upon Solomon’s ring, peace be upon him.

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that it is written at the beginning of every sūrah of the Noble Qurʾān. Among its special properties is that if a person recites it 786 times—the number the source associates with its letters—for seven consecutive days with an intention for a matter, he will obtain all of that: bringing good, warding off evil, or [UNCLEAR: the source says “the marriage of merchandise,” then says that it marries by the permission of God].

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that whoever recites it twenty-one times at bedtime will be protected by God Most High that night from accursed Satan, theft, and sudden death, and every affliction will be kept away from him.

Among its special properties is that if it is recited fifty times in the face of a tyrant, God Most High will humble him, cast its awe into that tyrant’s heart, and grant safety from his evil.

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that if it is recited at sunrise three hundred times while you face the Sun, together with invoking blessings upon the Prophet the same number of times, God Most High will provide for him from where he does not expect, and a year will not pass before he becomes completely wealthy.

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm for love and affection is that if it is recited over a cup of water 786 times and the water is given to whoever you wish, that person will love him intensely. If he drinks that water at sunrise for seven days, his dullness will disappear and he will retain everything he hears. [UNCLEAR: the source’s pronouns are ambiguous.]

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that if it is recited sixty-one times when rain falls, with the intention of seeking rain, God Most High will complete it. [UNCLEAR: the object of “complete it” is not specified.]

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that if it is recited after the dawn prayer two thousand five hundred times, with sincere intention and a humble heart, for forty days, God Most High will pour upon its reciter some of the hidden secrets. He will see in his sleep everything that occurs in the world. This requires spiritual discipline; he will see wonders, and he should keep his secret concealed.

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm for fulfilling needs and entering the presence of rulers is that whoever wants this should fast on Thursday, [UNCLEAR: the source says to “look upon oil and dates”], perform the sunset prayer, and recite it one hundred and twenty-one times. Then he should recite it without counting until sleep overcomes him. When he rises on Friday, he should pray the dawn prayer, recite it the stated number of times, and write it on paper with musk, saffron, and rose water. He should fumigate it with ʿūd and ambergris and write it the stated number of times.

“By God, besides whom there is no deity, no man or woman carries it without becoming, in people’s eyes, like the full moon. He becomes honored, awe-inspiring, eminent, and obeyed. Everyone who sees him loves him, fulfills his need, and casts love for him into the hearts of creation.

“This is the method for writing it: write Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm one hundred and twenty-one times, with the writing joined together.

“Another method: write it on gazelle parchment one hundred and twenty-one times with musk, saffron, rose water, and incense of costus, mastic, frankincense, and benzoin. The person afflicted in his provision should carry it; God will open matters for him and expand his provision. If a debtor carries it, God Most High will pay his debt, and it will be a protection for him from every disliked thing. If he writes it in a glass bowl forty times, erases it with Zamzam water or sweet well water, and drinks from that…”

Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm tertulis di dahi Adam lima ratus tahun sebelum ia diciptakan. Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm tertulis di sayap Jibril pada hari ia turun kepada Ibrahim, semoga keselamatan atas keduanya. Ia berkata: “Dengan nama Allah: wahai api, jadilah dingin dan keselamatan bagi Ibrahim.” Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm juga tertulis pada tongkat Musa, semoga keselamatan atasnya. Tulisannya menggunakan bahasa Suryani; seandainya bukan karenanya, laut tidak akan terbelah untuknya.

Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm berada pada lisan Isa, semoga keselamatan atasnya, ketika ia berbicara di dalam buaian. Ia membacakannya kepada orang-orang mati, lalu mereka hidup dengan izin Allah Yang Mahatinggi. Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm tertulis pada cincin Sulaiman, semoga keselamatan atasnya.

Di antara khawāṣṣ Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm adalah bahwa ia tertulis pada awal setiap surah Al-Qur’an yang mulia. Di antara khawāṣṣ-nya adalah bahwa apabila seseorang membacanya 786 kali—angka yang oleh sumber dikaitkan dengan huruf-hurufnya—selama tujuh hari berturut-turut dengan niat untuk suatu perkara, ia akan memperoleh semua itu: mendatangkan kebaikan, menolak keburukan, atau [UNCLEAR: sumber menyebut “menikahkan barang”, lalu mengatakan bahwa ia menikah dengan izin Allah].

Di antara khawāṣṣ Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm adalah bahwa barang siapa membacanya dua puluh satu kali ketika hendak tidur akan diamankan oleh Allah Yang Mahatinggi pada malam itu dari setan terkutuk, pencurian, dan kematian mendadak; setiap bala akan dijauhkan darinya.

Di antara khawāṣṣ-nya adalah bahwa apabila ia dibaca lima puluh kali di hadapan seorang zalim, Allah Yang Mahatinggi akan merendahkannya, melemparkan kewibawaan bacaan itu ke dalam hati orang zalim tersebut, dan memberikan keselamatan dari kejahatannya.

Di antara khawāṣṣ Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm adalah bahwa apabila ia dibaca tiga ratus kali ketika matahari terbit sementara engkau menghadap matahari, disertai selawat kepada Nabi dengan jumlah yang sama, Allah Yang Mahatinggi akan memberinya rezeki dari arah yang tidak ia sangka, dan setahun tidak akan berlalu sebelum ia menjadi kaya sepenuhnya.

Di antara khawāṣṣ Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm untuk cinta dan kasih sayang adalah bahwa apabila ia dibacakan di atas secangkir air sebanyak 786 kali lalu air itu diberikan kepada siapa pun yang engkau kehendaki, orang tersebut akan mencintainya dengan cinta yang sangat kuat. Jika ia meminum air itu ketika matahari terbit selama tujuh hari, kebodohannya akan hilang dan ia akan mengingat segala sesuatu yang didengarnya. [UNCLEAR: kata ganti dalam sumber tidak jelas.]

Di antara khawāṣṣ Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm adalah bahwa apabila ia dibaca enam puluh satu kali ketika hujan turun, dengan niat memohon hujan, Allah Yang Mahatinggi akan menyempurnakannya. [UNCLEAR: objek dari “menyempurnakannya” tidak disebutkan.]

Di antara khawāṣṣ Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm adalah bahwa apabila ia dibaca setelah salat Subuh dua ribu lima ratus kali, dengan niat yang tulus dan hati yang khusyuk, selama empat puluh hari, Allah Yang Mahatinggi akan melimpahkan kepada pembacanya sebagian rahasia yang tersembunyi. Ia akan melihat dalam tidurnya segala sesuatu yang terjadi di dunia. Hal itu mensyaratkan riyāḍah; ia akan melihat keajaiban, dan hendaklah ia menyembunyikan rahasianya.

Di antara khawāṣṣ Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm untuk menunaikan hajat dan menghadap para penguasa adalah bahwa siapa pun yang menghendakinya hendaklah berpuasa pada hari Kamis, [UNCLEAR: sumber mengatakan agar ia “melihat minyak dan kurma”], melaksanakan salat Magrib, dan membacanya seratus dua puluh satu kali. Kemudian hendaklah ia membacanya tanpa hitungan sampai rasa kantuk menguasainya. Ketika bangun pada hari Jumat, hendaklah ia melaksanakan salat Subuh, membacanya dengan jumlah yang telah disebutkan, dan menulisnya di atas kertas dengan misik, za‘faran, dan air mawar. Hendaklah ia mengasapinya dengan ʿūd dan ambergris serta menulisnya dengan jumlah yang telah disebutkan.

“Demi Allah, yang tiada tuhan selain Dia, tidak ada laki-laki atau perempuan yang membawanya kecuali ia akan menjadi, di mata manusia, seperti Bulan purnama. Ia menjadi mulia, berwibawa, terpandang, dan ditaati. Setiap orang yang melihatnya akan mencintainya, menunaikan hajatnya, dan menanamkan cintanya di dalam hati makhluk.

“Beginilah cara menulisnya: tulislah Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm seratus dua puluh satu kali, dengan tulisan yang tersambung.

“Cara lain: tulislah ia pada kulit kijang seratus dua puluh satu kali dengan misik, za‘faran, air mawar, dan dupa qist, mi‘ah, kemenyan, dan benzoin. Orang yang mengalami kesempitan rezeki hendaklah membawanya; Allah akan membukakan jalan baginya dan meluaskan rezekinya. Jika orang yang berutang membawanya, Allah Yang Mahatinggi akan melunasi utangnya dan ia menjadi perlindungan baginya dari segala hal yang tidak disukai. Jika ia menulisnya di dalam mangkuk kaca empat puluh kali, menghapusnya dengan air Zamzam atau air sumur yang tawar, lalu meminum dari air itu…”

[UNCLEAR: the page begins with “the water,” continuing the preceding instruction.] Any sick person who drinks it will be healed by God Most High. If a woman having difficulty giving birth drinks from it, she will deliver immediately.

If it is written on a sheet of paper thirty-five times and hung in a house, no Satan or jinn will enter it and blessing will increase there. If that sheet is hung in a shop, its customers, profit, and merchandise will increase, and it will blind the eyes of onlookers.

If it is written on a sheet one hundred and seven times on the first day of Muḥarram and a person carries it, no harm will befall him or the members of his household for the duration of his life.

If it is written one hundred and ten times for a woman whose children do not survive, or for a barren woman who has not yet conceived, after she has been purified from menstruation for three days, and she carries the sheet and her husband has intercourse with her, she will conceive by the permission of God Most High. She should not put down the sheet after sixty days; she will bear a righteous child and will experience no pain or hardship in bearing it, by the permission of God Most High.

If it is written sixty-one times and carried by a woman whose children do not survive, her children will live. This has been tested and confirmed, and God is powerful over all things.

If it is written on a sheet one hundred and one times and buried in a crop, that crop will become fertile and be protected from all pests. If it is written seventy times and placed with the dead person in his shroud, he will be safe from the terror of Munkar and Nakīr, and it will be a light for him until the Day of Resurrection.

If it is written on a lead tablet and placed in a fisherman’s net, his catch will increase. If it is written once on a card and placed beneath the bezel of a ring, and the ring is placed in [UNCLEAR: a liquid the source calls “menstrual milk”] and a person bitten by poison drinks it, [UNCLEAR: the source’s following wording is damaged]; the poison will leave him by the permission of God Most High.

If its letters are written separately and carried, it will have great virtue. The bāʾ is God’s splendor; the sīn is His radiance; the mīm is His glory and dominion; the alif is His pre-eternity; the lām is His gentleness; the hāʾ is His guidance; the alif is His command; the lām is [UNCLEAR: associated in the source with “the alām of dominion”]; the rāʾ is His mercy; the ḥāʾ is His wisdom; the mīm is His kingdom; and the nūn is His favor.

[UNCLEAR: the source then gives a damaged instruction to write a form of the basmalah beginning with the letter bāʾ twenty-one times and place it among one’s wealth, increasing its blessing.] For protection, write this number and add to it the following verse, whose letters are given as: “Peace upon Noah among the worlds.” Erase it and give it to the poisoned person to drink; he will be cured immediately by the permission of God Most High.

Whoever writes it on a sheet of paper and looks at the letter mīm forty times every day while saying, “O God, Owner of the dominion,” up to the words “in Your hand is the good,” will not know from where good comes to him, and God will bless what is before him.

Whoever writes al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm fifty times on a sheet, recites the basmalah over it one hundred and fifty times, carries it, and enters before a ruler or tyrant will be safe from his evil and no harm will befall him.

Whoever writes al-Raḥmān on a knife [UNCLEAR: the source’s phrase about its making and purpose is damaged], recites over it three hundred and thirty-one times, slaughters a rooster with it, and separates its head from its body—when the source’s unclear condition concerning the head occurs, take the head and bury it beneath the threshold of the door of the desired house. If the rooster’s head is fried in good oil and the person suffering pain is anointed with it, it will benefit him greatly. If a bleeding woman carries it, it will benefit her greatly.

Whoever writes al-Raḥīm on a banner one hundred and ninety times, carries it, and enters a battle, no weapon will affect him and no illness will befall him. [UNCLEAR: the page ends with the incomplete fragment “and whoever…”].

[UNCLEAR: halaman dimulai dengan “air itu”, sebagai kelanjutan instruksi sebelumnya.] Orang sakit mana pun yang meminumnya akan disembuhkan oleh Allah Yang Mahatinggi. Jika perempuan yang mengalami kesulitan melahirkan meminumnya, ia akan melahirkan seketika.

Apabila ia ditulis pada selembar kertas tiga puluh lima kali lalu digantung di rumah, setan dan jin tidak akan memasukinya dan keberkahan akan bertambah di sana. Apabila kertas itu digantung di sebuah toko, pelanggan, keuntungan, dan barang dagangannya akan bertambah, serta mata orang-orang yang melihatnya akan dibutakan.

Apabila ia ditulis pada selembar kertas seratus tujuh kali pada hari pertama Muharram lalu dibawa seseorang, tidak ada hal buruk yang akan menimpanya atau anggota keluarganya selama hidupnya.

Apabila ia ditulis seratus sepuluh kali untuk perempuan yang anak-anaknya tidak bertahan hidup, atau perempuan mandul yang belum hamil, setelah ia bersuci dari haid selama tiga hari, lalu ia membawa kertas itu dan suaminya menyetubuhinya, ia akan hamil dengan izin Allah Yang Mahatinggi. Ia tidak boleh meletakkan kertas itu setelah enam puluh hari; ia akan melahirkan anak yang saleh dan tidak mengalami rasa sakit atau kesulitan dalam mengandungnya, dengan izin Allah Yang Mahatinggi.

Apabila ia ditulis enam puluh satu kali dan dibawa oleh perempuan yang anak-anaknya tidak bertahan hidup, anak-anaknya akan hidup. Hal itu telah diuji dan terbukti, dan Allah Mahakuasa atas segala sesuatu.

Apabila ia ditulis pada selembar kertas seratus satu kali lalu dikuburkan di tanaman, tanaman itu akan menjadi subur dan terlindung dari semua hama. Apabila ia ditulis tujuh puluh kali lalu diletakkan bersama mayat di dalam kain kafannya, ia akan aman dari kedahsyatan Munkar dan Nakīr dan tulisan itu akan menjadi cahaya baginya sampai Hari Kebangkitan.

Apabila ia ditulis pada lempeng timah lalu diletakkan di jaring nelayan, tangkapannya akan bertambah. Write it on a sheet of paper twenty-one times and hang it on a person suffering from headache; it will benefit him. Whoever writes it on seven almonds with a yellow-copper needle on Friday during the hour of Venus, recites the name its prescribed number of times over the almonds, and feeds them to whomever he wishes, will make that person love him intensely.

Whoever writes it in this manner on a new mirror on Monday at sunrise, and the person called ṣāḥib al-lūqah [UNCLEAR: the term is obscure] looks at himself in it frequently, may God Most High heal him. Whoever writes al-rīḥī [UNCLEAR: the term is obscure] in this manner on a silver ring weighing two dirhams and carries it with him will be granted awe and obedience by God Most High.

Whoever wants to subdue every tyrant should write a wafq of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm on a piece of lead, place the name of the person desired in the wafq, fumigate it with khintīt and red garlic, and bury it near a fire with continuously burning fuel. Beware of letting the fire touch the lead, for the working will be destroyed and you will be held accountable for it before God Most High. This is its form, as you see:

| Bism | Allah | al-Raḥmān | al-Raḥīm | Fulan |
| Allah | al-Raḥmān | al-Raḥīm | Fulan | Bism |
| al-Raḥmān | al-Raḥīm | Fulan | Bism | Allah |
| Fulan | Bism | Allah | al-Raḥmān | al-Raḥīm |

This is what you recite over it: “Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm; Bismillah al-Ḥayy al-Qayyūm, before whom faces bow, voices become humble, and hearts tremble out of fear of Him. I ask You to bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, his family, and his Companions, and to grant my need concerning Fulan. O God, You know that if he turns back from what he is doing, then guide him and grant him success; but if You know that he will not turn back, send down upon him Your affliction and wrath and destroy him—O Qāhir, O Qahhār, O Qādir, O Muqtadir, O God”—seven times. Supplicate with this seven hundred times. The wrongdoer will either turn back from his wrongdoing or perish quickly. So fear God Most High.

Whoever writes the noble basmalah eight times in the center of a circle, writes around it the Most High’s words, “Muḥammad is the Messenger of God and those with him…” to the end of the sūrah, fumigates it with a pleasant fragrance at a fortunate time, and carries it will become feared, magnified, and honored among people. Everyone who sees him will love him and naturally incline toward him, and all his aims will succeed by the permission of God Most High.

Whoever writes the entire basmalah while the Moon is in Pisces and the ascendant is fortunate, on gazelle parchment, and carries it on his head with its prescribed number [UNCLEAR: the source’s phrase about the number is obscure], will live happily and die a martyr. He will see nothing in himself, his wealth, or his child that he dislikes.

Know—may God grant me and you success in obeying Him—that “Bism” is the concealed name, and God Most High is the Greatest Name. al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is an attribute by which He describes Himself: He is the Merciful of this world and the Merciful of the Hereafter.

“Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds” corresponds to “Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm.” Thus “Bismillah” corresponds to “Praise be to God,” and “al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm” corresponds to “Lord of the worlds.” Know that every attribute of His in the saying “Master of the Day of Judgment” is a manifestation of lordship: He is King and Owner. [UNCLEAR: the source then discusses clarifying the words and lights, seeking on the Day of Judgment, and the attributive quality of ownership.]

Through the attribute of ownership He becomes King of kings and manifests to souls through subjugation, victory, and kingship. [UNCLEAR: the source then repeats that He is King of kings and manifests to hearts through ownership.] This corresponds to His saying, “In the presence of a Powerful Sovereign.”

All of this is contained in Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm. “Bismillah,” which is the Name, [UNCLEAR: the source says that it conveys the comprehensive words toward “the end by the truth” and raises the call with a tongue of divine turning toward God in ascent]. The lāhūt of al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm descends to the second beginning, while Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm ascends to the first beginning.

Within it is the secret of beginning and the ranks of divine unity, because “Bism” corresponds to “I bear witness,” and “Allah” corresponds to “there is no deity except Him.” It contains the ranks of the angels corresponding to al-Raḥmān and those endowed with knowledge corresponding to al-Raḥīm.

Likewise, there is the relation of the quadrangular world, which is expressed in the saying of al-Raḥmān, Most High: “Those are the ones upon whom God has bestowed favor, from among the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous”—from the raḥīmiyyah to the raḥmāniyyah. Therefore the degrees are reached in the ascent to Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm. [UNCLEAR: the page ends with the incomplete word “first…”.]
